criteria.statement: An MCP write uses BuildIntentEvent and ProcessInProcess with the NIP-98 principal pubkey as actor and TrustSet authorization.
A stable progressToken or idempotency key deduplicates a retry and preserves the original event correlation.
Accepted writes return signed canonical state, rejected writes return structured errors, and unavailable state returns a successful pending correlation.
Every registered MCP write tool uses the intent processor and obsolete ContextVM publisher dependencies and async publish functions are removed.
Every migrated tool has accepted, rejected, replay and pending pipeline tests.
